IDEA: HYSPLIT-BEHV-RQ
TITLE: Behaviour-contrast hyperbolic dyadic refinement of the deepest RQ codebook
MOTIVATION: The two negative rounds both lost recall exactly when deep prefix capacity fell (2201 distinct L3 prefixes → 0.0544; 1298 → 0.0517), and both lost capacity by moving input points toward a behaviour hub. The behaviour signal that does predict recall on the 107 confirmed pairs is behaviour-CONTRAST, not Gromov-delta, not ancestor depth. So the useful place for behaviour is not the item position (it merges) but the DEEP CODEBOOK: let the deepest level be doubled into behaviour-polarized child codewords whose offsets are measured from the training transition contrast, so the level-3 partition becomes strictly finer and the extra tokens carry behaviour rather than duplicating it.
NOVELTY: Round one/two moved items and residuals (merging). The rejected ideas ranked items radially (BRad-RQ), set curvature from a prefix-transition score (CURVCTRL-SID), used successor-weighted Fréchet codebook means (poincare-frechet-successor-codebook), or built cones/tree-embeddings. None of them *generated extra codewords* from a behaviour statistic. Here no point moves; the codebook itself is refined by a measured behaviour contrast through the Poincaré exponential map, doubling deep-level capacity at zero free parameters (the offsets are buffers, not trained), so it cannot collapse to the origin and cannot over-merge.
CHANGE: Replace the deepest level's K-codeword nearest-neighbour by a 2K structured codebook: each anchor codeword c_k spawns two children exp_{c_k}(±rho_k u_k), where u_k is the EMA of the mean behaviour-contrast vector of the items currently assigned to anchor k and rho_k is the EMA of the median absolute tangent projection of those items on u_k. Anchor selection and child selection are both hyperbolic nearest-neighbour, so the level-3 token is a function of the behaviour-derived child placements.
SPECIFICATION: Fix c=1 (curvature is a gauge; fixing it costs no generality). Levels 1..L-1 are untouched. For level L with anchor codebook {c_k} in the Poincare ball:
  p_i = exp_0(r_i) ; a_i = argmin_k d_c(p_i, c_k)
  u_k <- normalize( (1-beta) u_k + beta * (1/m_k) * sum_{i in A_k} btilde_i )
  rho_k <- (1-beta) rho_k + beta * median_{i in A_k} |<log_{c_k}(p_i), u_k>|
  c_{k,+} = exp_{c_k}(+rho_k u_k), c_{k,-} = exp_{c_k}(-rho_k u_k)
  pi_i = argmin_{pi in {+,-}} d_c(p_i, c_{a_i,pi}) ; token_i = 2*a_i + (pi_i+1)/2
with beta = 1/24 (one-epoch window, derived from 24 steps/epoch), u_k, rho_k stop-gradient EMA buffers, updated after each optimizer step. btilde_i is the fixed-seed projected contrast from the train split only. rho_k is capped at 0.5 * median_k min_{k'!=k} d_c(c_k, c_k') (measured codebook spacing; the pair may not overlap a neighbouring Voronoi cell).
COST: +K extra level-L codeword embeddings in Stage 2 (K*D parameters, e.g. 256*64 = 16k) and +K extra SID token rows in the Stage-3 embedding table. Per step at frozen scale: batch ~1023 items (24556 items / 24 steps), one log map and 2K-way distance evaluation at level L, ~2*1023*2K*D ~ 1.3e8 FLOPs, i.e. well under 1% of the encoder/decoder pass. One-time precompute of btilde over 24556 items is O(nnz(transitions)*D). Expected Stage-2 epoch time 0.150-0.163 s on four GPUs, inside the measured budget.
HYPOTHESIS: If deep-prefix merging is what cost rounds one and two, and if behaviour contrast is the discriminative behaviour signal, then this mechanism should raise distinct L3 token usage from ~K to >1.5K, leave the L1/L2 prefix counts at the baseline level (~251/1769), and push Stage-3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 (target: at or above the 0.0679 frozen baseline) in one run. Worth keeping if L3 distinct tokens rise materially while L1/L2 stay flat and recall does not regress; the decisive observation is test_recall@10 > 0.065 with recall@5 and ndcg@10 moving consistently.
RISKS: Contrast may be zero or near-zero for many items (isolated, cold, or symmetric items), leaving one child per anchor unused and the gain near zero. The fixed random projection of the contrast may be misaligned with the directions the encoder actually uses. Placing children off the anchor raises the level-L reconstruction error if the argmin does not compensate. Since levels 1..L-1 are untouched, if the true bottleneck is L1/L2 granularity the gain is capped. A moving codebook during the 3000-epoch schedule can chase the EMA; a one-epoch window mitigates but may oscillate. Anchors near the ball boundary get strongly curved children.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item-transition contrast per item: the difference between the item's successor distribution and its predecessor distribution, i.e. how much it is a "source" vs a "sink" in the training transition graph.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the Stage-2 TRAINING split only: A_ij = number of times item j occurs immediately after item i in a training sequence (window 1). Row-normalize to p_out(i), column-normalize to p_in(i), b_i = p_out(i) - p_in(i) (sparse, length |I|). Project once with a fixed Gaussian matrix G in R^{D x |I|}, G_ab ~ N(0,1/D), seeded by the recipe's data seed: btilde_i = G b_i, set to 0 if ||btilde_i|| < 1e-8. Computed before Stage 2 starts and frozen for the whole run.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: btilde uses only training-split sequences and is frozen before any Stage-2 step; no validation or test sequence is read. beta, the curvature (=1), the projection seed and the 0.5 spacing factor are fixed a priori; the only data-dependent constant, the spacing bound, is measured from the current train-fitted codebook, never from validation recall. Stage 3 receives only the frozen SID file and never re-reads behaviour. No hyperparameter is selected by validation.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature c = 1 (gauge-fixed, since scaling the tangent by 1/sqrt(c) reproduces c=1 exactly): Poincare distance d_c, exponential map exp_{c_k} on the tangent space at an anchor, and logarithmic map log_{c_k} used to measure the contrast projection. Applied at the deepest quantizer level only.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Inside the residual quantizer's deepest assignment step (curved quantization): it decides both the anchor (Poincare nearest neighbour) and the child codeword position (Poincare exponential map from the anchor), and thus the level-L SID token emitted to Stage 3.
COUPLING PATH: train-only transition contrast btilde -> per-anchor EMA mean direction u_k and EMA median tangent extent rho_k -> child codeword positions exp_{c_k}(±rho_k u_k) in the ball -> Poincare nearest child -> level-L SID token -> Stage-3 token sequence. Behaviour alone without the curved exp/log would give a flat Euclidean offset with no anchor-local frame; geometry alone without behaviour gives u_k = 0 and rho_k = 0, so the two children coincide and the computation collapses exactly to the K-codeword baseline. Removing either changes the emitted tokens.
COUPLING EQUATION: token_i = 2 * argmin_k d_c(p_i, c_k) + [ argmin_{pi in {+,-}} d_c(p_i, exp_{c_{a_i}}(pi * rho_{a_i} * u_{a_i})) ], with u_{a} = normalize(EMA[ mean_{i in A_a} btilde_i ]) and rho_a = EMA[ median_{i in A_a} |<log_{c_a}(p_i), u_a>| ]; the behaviour term is btilde_i inside u_a and rho_a, the curved term is d_c and exp_{c_a}.
OBSERVABLES: number of distinct level-L tokens actually used (expect ~K -> >1.5K), L1/L2 prefix counts (expect ~unchanged at ~251/~1769), per-anchor child-usage entropy and fraction of anchors with both children used, Stage-2 reconstruction curve, then Stage-3 test_recall@10, recall@5, ndcg@10, plus the recorded behaviour diagnostics (consecutive-SID transition adjacency and prefix transfer predictability).
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: identical code path with the contrast switch set so btilde_i = 0 for all items; then u_k = 0, rho_k = 0, both children equal c_k, the argmin ties resolve to '+' and the level-L alphabet is effectively K, i.e. the plain baseline quantizer at that depth.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: identical code path with Euclidean replacements exp(v) = c + v, log(z) = z - c, d = d_E; children sit at c_k ± rho_k u_k and both anchor and child selection are Euclidean nearest neighbour, with all behaviour statistics unchanged.
ABLATION BOTH ON: full mechanism, fixed c = 1 Poincare exp/log/distance with the contrast-derived children; this is the single trained arm.
SPEC EQUATIONS: 
  exp_0(r) = tanh(||r||/2) * r/||r||, exp_c(v) = c (+) tanh(||v||/2) * v/||v||
  d_c(p,q) = arcosh(1 + 2||p-q||^2 / ((1-||p||^2)(1-||q||^2)))
  log_c(z) = 2 * artanh(||(-c) (+) z||) * ((-c) (+) z)/||(-c) (+) z||
  step(t):
    z <- Encoder(x) ; (levels 1..L-1 quantized as baseline) ; r <- residual
    p <- exp_0(r) ; a <- argmin_k d_c(p, c_k)
    pi <- argmin_{+-} d_c(p, exp_{c_a}(+- rho_a u_a)) ; j <- 2a + (pi+1)/2
    zhat <- Decoder(quantized(z, j)) ; loss <- baseline reconstruction loss (unchanged)
  after optimizer step:
    for each k with m_k = |A_k| > 0:
      s <- mean_{i in A_k} btilde_i ; u_k <- normalize((1-beta)u_k + beta s)
      r <- median_{i in A_k} |<log_{c_k}(p_i), u_k>| ; rho_k <- (1-beta)rho_k + beta r
    dn <- median_k min_{k'!=k} d_c(c_k, c_k') ; rho_k <- min(rho_k, 0.5*dn)
  beta = 1/24, c = 1, u_k(0) = 0, rho_k(0) = 0
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: per-item deepest-level residual r_i (or encoder latent), anchor codebook {c_k} from the baseline recipe, per-item frozen contrast btilde_i, buffers u_k and rho_k, curvature c = 1, beta = 1/24. Outputs: level-L token index j_i in [0, 2K), quantized vector exp_{c_{a_i}}(pi_i rho_{a_i} u_{a_i}), and updated buffers; the SID becomes (level 1..L-1 tokens, j_i).
SAFEGUARDS: fix c = 1 (gauge) so no curvature tuning exists; clip ||p|| to 1-1e-5 and the arcosh argument to >= 1+1e-12 before every d_c/log_c; Möbius addition keeps exp_c inside the ball by construction, and rho_k is additionally capped at half the measured median nearest-anchor spacing so children cannot cross into a neighbouring cell; if any buffer is non-finite keep its previous value; anchors with m_k = 0 keep their buffers and emit only their '+' child so the alphabet never breaks; sign(0) resolves to '+'; buffers are stop-gradient so no new gradient path can destabilise the encoder; the new token ids are appended to both the Stage-2 codebook table and the Stage-3 SID vocabulary with a fixed offset.
END IDEA
